ashley-eng: FYI noticed a case where a tenant with a large reserved reservation (90% of node) pushes synthetic traffic and another tenant gets effectively zero egress. isolation config says 'soft-isolate' but behavior looked hard-blocking. anyone seen this?
kevin-sre: saw similar yesterday in canary. looks like our 'elastic reservation' falls back to fill-unreserved but we also mark inflight slots as reserved immediately which starves neighbors.
maria-platform: can you paste the trace? need to see routing decisions + node-level counters. telemetry should show reservation_held vs reservation_used.
ashley-eng: pasted logs — snippet below from router: 
```
ROUTER INFO route=dedicated node=n3 tenant=tenant-A action=claim-reservation reserved_slots=72 inflight=85
ROUTER INFO route=dedicated node=n3 tenant=tenant-B action=defer reason=reservation-held
```
kevin-sre: that 'inflight=85' is the bug — we count inflight as reserved until completion. should be reserved_slots + pending-ack only.
sam-ml: interesting edge: model warmup requests inflate inflight briefly, so a tenant can 'grab' capacity while not actually consuming long-term tokens. this makes soft caps look like hard caps.
maria-platform: UX/console impact: customers see 'dedicated capacity saturated' and open support tickets. we should expose a new metric: 'reservation_utilization' = used / reserved. put a threshold and an alert.
jont-console: +1 on metric. also propose showing per-tenant pending-warmup in the Tenants view and a small tooltip: "pending warmups may temporarily block other tenants".
olivia-ux: for rollout UX, we should not surface raw counters to customers immediately. prefer a computed status: OK / Degraded (soft limit) / Isolated (hard). default to Degraded when reservation_utilization < 0.6 but nodes show high inflight spikes.
kevin-sre: proposal for enforcement change: decouple 'claim' from 'consume'. Claim should be a cheap reservation token with TTL (e.g., 2s). only when worker ack arrives do we convert token->consumed. if TTL expires, release token and let neighbors use. this prevents warmup grabs.
ambernote: deploy-bot: rollout started for change 'routing/soft-reservation-ttl' to canary.
ashley-eng: sounds good. does anyone see scenarios where short TTL could cause oscillation and thrash?
sam-ml: if model cold starts oscillate across tenants, short TTL might drop useful reservations. mitigations: backoff retries and exponential hold for successive attempts.
maria-platform: telemetry additions we need: reservation_tokens_issued, reservation_tokens_released, reservation_tokens_expired, reservation_tokens_converted. dashboards: per-node and per-tenant stacks.
kevin-sre: can we add a quick config snippet?
```json
{
  "reservation_policy": {
    "mode": "soft",
    "claim_ttl_ms": 2000,
    "max_pending_per_tenant": 10,
    "convert_on_worker_ack": true
  }
}
```
kevin-sre: default keeps soft mode but prevents permanent grabs.
jont-console: for console UX, add a 'safety-net' toggle per-tenant (on by default) that enforces claim_ttl and shows an "expired claims" counter. also add a one-click 'override for this tenant' for enterprise customers.
olivia-ux: mockups later this afternoon. will include inline help copy explaining "why your neighbor saw degraded throughput". short copy only.
maria-platform: action items: (1) kevin implement claim_ttl logic + telemetry (2) sam add warmup backoff heuristic (3) jon add dashboard panels (4) olivia mockups / copy (5) ashley schedule canary and draft release notes.
kevin-sre: i'll open PR and link it here. expect initial canary tomorrow.
ashley-eng: thanks — please ping #oncall when canary goes live so support awareness. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued by kevin-sre for change routing/soft-reservation-ttl -> canary-group-3
